panels.description: Hardware-reported CPU utilization percentage as measured by the iDRAC.
panels.title: CPU Utilization (%)

panels.description: Hardware-reported CPU utilization as exported by the iDRAC.
panels.title: CPU Usage

panels.description: Average processor clock frequency across all cores, in MHz as reported by the iDRAC. A drop without a matching drop in utilization indicates frequency scaling or throttling.
panels.title: Avg Core Frequency (MHz)

panels.description: Overall memory subsystem utilization reported by the iDRAC.
panels.title: Memory Utilization

panels.description: Overall I/O subsystem utilization reported by the iDRAC.
panels.title: I/O Utilization

panels.description: Share of time cores spend in the active C0 state. A low value with high utilization suggests cores are being parked or throttled.
panels.title: C0 Residency

panels.description: CPU utilization from both the percentage reading and the raw usage metric. Divergence between the two can indicate a reporting or firmware issue.
panels.title: CPU Utilization Over Time

panels.description: Real-time processor clock frequency averaged across all cores. Sustained drops while utilization stays high point to power capping or thermal throttling.
panels.title: Average Core Frequency

panels.description: Memory and I/O subsystem utilization. Sustained saturation here is a common source of application latency.
panels.title: Memory & I/O Utilization

panels.description: CPU utilization overlaid with average core frequency. When utilization rises but frequency falls, the processor is being throttled rather than scaling up.
panels.title: Frequency vs Utilization

panels.description: Frequency reductions imposed on the CPU by power caps or thermal limits during the selected time range.
panels.title: CPU Limiting Events

panels.description: Frequency reductions imposed on the memory subsystem (DDR) by power caps or thermal limits during the selected time range.
panels.title: DDR Limiting Events

panels.description: Instances where the CPU breached a power or thermal ceiling during the selected time range.
panels.title: CPU Violations

panels.description: Total power and thermal limiting events recorded during the selected time range.
panels.title: Limiting Events

panels.description: Processor package thermal status as reported by the iDRAC. 0 = OK, 1 = Warning, 2 = Critical.
panels.title: Package Thermal Status

panels.description: Thermal control circuit (PROCHOT) activation. When active, the processor is being throttled to protect itself from overheating.
panels.title: Thermal Control Circuit (PROCHOT)

panels.description: Rate of CPU and DDR frequency limiting events. Any sustained non-zero rate means the workload is being capped by power or thermal limits.
panels.title: CPU & DDR Limiting Rate

panels.description: Rate of power/thermal ceiling violations and total limiting events. Correlate spikes with workload changes or ambient temperature increases.
panels.title: Violations & Limiting Events Rate

panels.description: Package thermal status and PROCHOT activation over time. A value of 1 on PROCHOT means the processor is actively throttling.
panels.title: Thermal Throttling Indicators

panels.description: Processor sleep state distribution. C0 is the active state; non-C0 covers all deeper sleep states. High non-C0 residency with high utilization indicates cores are being parked.
panels.title: C0 vs Non-C0 Residency

panels.description: Current split between active (C0) and sleep (non-C0) residency per server.
panels.title: Residency Distribution
